key_insight: Objective-level evaluation can misrank mechanistic circuits: a circuit that scores better on faithfulness can actually reproduce model behavior worse than an equally sized alternative.
engineering_relevance: For mechanistic interpretability pipelines, improving the discovery algorithm is not enough unless the validation objective reliably tracks true behavioral recovery.
method: Compared validation faithfulness against held-out behavioral agreement under ordinary resampling across four human-reference tasks and InterpBench.
Tested controlled reference edits and outputs from EAP, EAP-IG, ACDC, and Edge-SP to expose misranking without relying on any single discovery method.
Analyzed context distortion by restoring excluded signals from the intact-model execution to see whether rankings could be repaired.
evidence_signal: Under resampling, KL misranked 9.4%–41.2% of candidate pairs on the human-reference tasks, and restoring selected signals fixed 96 of 100 persistent misrankings in the study pool.
watch_item: Faithfulness metrics can be sensitive to distribution shifts caused by exclusion-based interventions, so validation setups must check whether the retained subcircuit is being evaluated on distorted inputs.
paper_title: Are We Recovering Mechanisms? Objective-Level Recovery Gaps in Mechanistic Interpretability
